At the academy, the otome game’s heroine suddenly confronts Linntia.

103509.synopsis:
Bai Xiaogu is a white bone that has become a spirit. One day, he discovers an extraordinary book titled “Those Years We Passionately Adored Tianyu Mountain’s Chief Qin Jiuqing.” After studying day and night, this simple bone spirit learns three profound truths:
First, spirits must cultivate to achieve greatness.
Second, dual cultivation is the fastest path forward.
Third, and most importantly, one needs the perfect partner with exceptional qualities – a supreme physique, powerful spiritual roots, eternal talent, boundless potential, and devastating good looks.
And as fate would have it, a certain Sword Sect Chief matches every single requirement.
The first step to dual cultivation is falling in love. So Bai Xiaogu clenches his bony fingers and declares: This bone wants to fall in love with Qin Jiuqing!
So the question is, how can this little bone spirit, who has finally managed to disguise himself as human and lurk in the cultivation world, attract the attention of the Sword Sect’s chief?
Qin Jiuqing, the youngest Sword Sect chief in the cultivation world, is the object of worship for countless cultivators. He is talented, good-looking, and his temperament is the epitome of coldness in the cultivation world – ice-type cultivators have expressed their fear of getting too close for fear of the cold.
Such an unattainable and flawless chief has but one tiny flaw.
“What? You’re saying Qin Jiuqing is poor?”
Are you kidding? Everyone knows Chief Qin’s cave is filled with glittering gold and treasures from heaven and earth, each harder than the last…
Well, if liking hard things counts as a flaw… then yes, Chief Qin does have one minor flaw.
He likes hard bones.
Literally hard bones.
The harder the better, and his favorites are the coldest white bones that have absorbed the essence of ghosts.
Bai Xiaogu: “???”
Qin Jiuqing: smiles faintly “That’s right, it’s you.”
One-sentence Summary: What’s wrong with white bones? White bones also want to fall in love~
Theme: The protagonist strives to carve out an alternative path of warmth in a world where the weak are preyed upon by the strong.
Author’s Note: The writing is humorous and witty, offering a non-human perspective on the world and experiencing the beauty of human emotions from a purer viewpoint. The narrative is heartwarming and sweet, with the two protagonists supporting each other and growing together. The plot is filled with ups and downs, telling a tale about time, space, and self in a fantastical world.

114517.synopsis:
On the immortal terrace grows a rare tree. Once every five hundred years, it bears a pair of twin fruits—both the reincarnated souls of immortal cultivators too obsessed, too stubborn, too damned to ever rest in peace. 
Xue Ranran, frail since birth, dragged her ghost of a life into the world of cultivation in the name of survival. Her last-ditch gamble? Apprenticing under Su Yishui—a prodigy cloaked in cold grace, lips sharp as his sword. 
From the moment she stepped across the sect’s threshold, the whispers never stopped. Su Yishui’s own master had once been the infamous demoness Mu Qingge—a woman soaked in sin, feared across realms, whose crimes piled so high even the heavens turned away. Two decades ago, Su Yishui led a righteous crusade to wipe her out, slicing his way through blood and betrayal, until the demon who raised him was dust scattered to the wind. 
Ranran? She played dumb, kept her head low, and stuffed her belly high. Life was already hell—why chase immortality when a warm meal and a cold drink hit harder? 
The sect teemed with beautiful senior brothers, dazzling enough to make her eyes sore. Her master, Su Yishui, may look like a fallen deity—but he wore frost like a second skin. 
Beautiful? Yes. Safe? Not at all. 
She had half a mind to run before he melted her spine into splinters. 
Rumor had it the demoness, Mu Qingge, had spent her twisted life pining for him. Wanted him. Couldn’t have him. But now she’s back—reborn, rebranded, practically dripping virtue—and ready to rekindle that forbidden flame. 
Ranran was charmed. Who wouldn’t be? This kind of twisted fairytale love was the stuff of legends. She even prepared a generous red envelope, planning to bless their messy reunion with silver and sarcasm. 
Until Su Yishui shoved her against a wall, close enough for his breath to fog up her bones. 
She stiffened, heart hammering, but bit back the tremble. “Immortal Master,” she said, voice low but defiant, “please, be loyal. Don’t let your lover down—again.” 
But Su Yishui only stared at her like he’d fallen into a dream he couldn’t claw out of. His voice was a broken whisper, soaked in obsession:
“Qingge… how much longer are you going to lie to me?”

115029.synopsis:
After transmigrating into a book, I fell in love with Ling Aorui, the one I was supposed to win over.
She was the heroine—powerful, beautiful, noble, and pure. She had almost no flaws, except for her blindness. After losing her sight, she became insecure and sensitive, and I saved her from several su*cide attempts.
I made a deal with the system to cure her eyes. The price was a shortened lifespan—I wouldn’t live more than ten years.

After her eyes were healed, she returned to the pinnacle of the Immortal Realm. The young masters from noble families who had previously ignored her now flocked to curry favor. This included Hua Jiaolian, the demonic sect’s enchantress who had once been her sworn enemy.
The two of them fought from morning till night, and then from night till morning. Eventually, when the enchantress was on the brink of death, she pulled Ling Aorui in by the waist and planted a retaliatory kiss on her.

She stayed by the enchantress’s bedside, caring for her meticulously, attending to her every need.

I leaped off the Immortal Execution Platform. When I woke up again, I was back on the day I first transmigrated. The system was chattering endlessly. I stopped it and said, “Forget it. I want to choose someone else.”
　　
*
Yu Yan had ascended a thousand years ago. Now, with nothing much happening in the Celestial Realm, she secretly transformed into a mere cultivator and went to the Immortal Realm to take a look.
Although it was an incarnation, it had a proper background. She was the long-reclusive mighty figure, Immortal Lord Minghuai. This Immortal Lord was famous for cultivating the Path of Heartlessness. With a frosty demeanor, calm and self-possessed, she disliked getting involved with others the most.
This suited her requirements perfectly: immortals and mortals should keep their distance, and she should maintain her purity.
Who knew that not long after she arrived, a voice came from the Celestial Realm.
—Because she had descended to the mortal world without permission, she had to undergo a love trial before she could return.

126549.synopsis:
In 19th-century England, Lyle, a war veteran who returned injured, visits Viscount Cliff to salvage his ruined family estate. Cliff offers to clear Lyle’s debts and reclaim his mortgaged home in exchange for Lyle relinquishing all rights to him and painting twenty paintings within a year. Lyle accepts the proposal.
While working as Cliff’s employee at the Clifford estate, painting as agreed, Lyle struggles with war trauma and repeatedly clashes with Cliff, who is unaware of his circumstances, causing emotional wounds. Cliff, disappointed by his first impression of Lyle, also harbors conflicting feelings toward him.
*
Deeply wounded in his pride, Cliff seized Lyle’s throat with both hands, gripping tightly. Yet, he couldn’t bring himself to press down with his thumbs. Acting on impulse, he was shocked by his own behavior, his hands trembling as they held Lyle’s neck. In his eyes, a whirlwind of countless emotions—love, resentment, fear, surprise, and hatred—flashed by.
Cliff’s face filled Lyle’s vision, a face torn between abandoning pride or holding onto it. Lyle, goading him, urged Cliff not to give up his pride.
“Would the esteemed Viscount of Clifford deign to dirty his hands with something so vulgar?”
Though his breath was constricted, the grip wasn’t tight enough to make him lose consciousness, so while it was painful, Lyle could endure it. He raised a hand and grabbed Cliff’s left wrist. As Cliff reacted, resisting forcefully, Lyle, as if to prove he hadn’t been using his full strength until now, seized Cliff’s wrist and pulled it downward.
Startled by Lyle’s immense grip strength, Cliff’s eyes silently questioned what he was trying to do. Lyle, as if to make a point, slid the captured hand down to Cliff’s left waist, where he grasped the holstered revolver along with Cliff’s hand.
“…You?”
As Cliff’s eyes widened in alarm, Lyle swiftly drew the revolver from the holster. The weapon, seemingly unused, had not a single scratch on its metal surface, and only one bullet was loaded in the five-chamber cylinder. Lyle capped the chamber with the single bullet and c*cked the hammer. At the click of the bullet locking into place, Cliff’s eyes grew even wider.
“Why go through the trouble of using your strength when you have this?”
“……”
“Does this feel familiar?”
